key_insight: Inter‑Stance provides a first-of-its-kind dyadic multimodal corpus that pairs synchronized audio/video/behavioral signals with self‑report measures to enable fine‑grained conversational stance analysis between interacting partners.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of publicly available datasets that capture multimodal recordings and participant self-reports from multi-person interactions, which has limited modeling of interpersonal stance dynamics and evaluation of conversational stance systems.
method: Record controlled dyadic conversations with synchronized multimodal streams (audio, video, facial/gesture cues) and transcripts.
Collect participant self‑report measures and turn-/time‑level stance annotations to create ground truth labels for interpersonal attitudes.
Process and align multimodal signals, define an annotation schema, and release the corpus with benchmarking tasks to support stance modeling and evaluation.
impact: Enables AI/ML researchers to train and evaluate multimodal models that capture how stance emerges and shifts in conversation, improving conversational agents, social signal processing, and human-centered interaction analysis.
visual_elements: Schematic of dyadic recording setup (two people + microphones/cameras) with icons for modalities (audio, video, face, gesture).
Multi‑track timeline showing synchronized streams (waveform, video thumbnails, gesture markers) with overlaid stance labels changing over time.
Annotation schema infographic (levels: self-report, turn-level, continuous) with example labeled utterance.
Benchmark snapshot: bar chart comparing baseline model performances on stance prediction tasks.
paper_title: Inter-Stance: A Dyadic Multimodal Corpus for Conversational Stance Analysis
paper_authors: Xiang Zhang, Xiaotian Li, Taoyue Wang, Nan Bi, Xin Zhou
